subject: QMon kickoff: initial integration plan, canary & rollback approach
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novamedical.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: QMon kickoff: initial integration plan, canary & rollback approach

Hi Olivia / Sam —

Thanks for agreeing to kick off the Quality Monitoring (QMon) integration with Redwood. Per our call last week, this thread will be our working thread for the CS -> Implementation handoff so the engineering and product teams have a single source of truth.

Attached: qmon-promptset-nova-v1.csv (initial prompt suite), eval-harness-webhook-config.yaml (example webhook that our harness can call), and a short runbook draft for canary/rollback steps.

Goal for this week:
- Align on the eval prompt set and tagging schema (safety / intent / clinical vs admin).
- Confirm where your eval harness will post judgment events (webhook URL or S3).
- Agree on canary policy and rollback triggers for model-serving changes.

From Redwood's side: Tessa will own implementation coordination, Monica will own ongoing QMon thresholds and alerts, and Jordan will be available for infra/deployment gating.

Can you confirm access to the Drive folder linked below (read for now), and whether the evaluation results will be pushed to a webhook we control, or if you prefer pulling from an S3 location?

Next steps (proposed):
1) Customer tech kickoff (30–45m) — this Thursday, 11/12 1:00pm PST.
2) We review the prompt set and tag mapping during the call.
3) We agree a canary window and an automated regression alert threshold (text/metric below).

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0119

Attachments: qmon-promptset-nova-v1.csv (32 prompts), eval-harness-webhook-config.yaml (2 KB), canary-rollback-runbook-v0.2.md (6 pages)

From: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novamedical.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samuel Price <sam.price@novamedical.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QMon kickoff: initial integration plan, canary & rollback approach

Marissa / Tessa —

Thanks for sending these files over. Drive access works for me (I confirmed read). We plan to run our internal eval harness and POST JSON verdicts to your webhook; Sam will add the payload schema shortly.

A few things from our side:
- Prompt set: we've included representative clinical and administrative prompts. We'll add two more clinically sensitive templates later today.
- SLOs: 95th percentile latency target for model responses is 2.5s; acceptable semantic-accuracy baseline for the initial model family is 0.82 (measured by our in-house annotators).
- Canary/rollback: we prefer a short canary (5% traffic for 2 hours) with an automated regression alert if the annotated accuracy drops more than 3% vs baseline or if a safety tag frequency increases above 1% absolute.

Sam (cc'd) — can you share the eval webhook endpoint details and a sample payload?

Olivia

--
Olivia Harper
Head of Product Integrations | Nova Medical
olivia.harper@novamedical.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novamedical.com>, Samuel Price <sam.price@novamedical.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T13:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QMon kickoff: initial integration plan, canary & rollback approach

Great — thanks for the quick confirmation, Olivia. Draft plan below (implementation owner in parentheses):

1) Tech kickoff (Tessa) — Thu 11/12 1:00pm PST (we'll use Zoom; link in Drive). Agenda: quick architecture walkthrough, prompt-set review, webhook schema validation, rollout gates.

2) Eval harness integration (Jordan + Sam) — by EOD Mon 11/15:
   - Verify webhook signature HMAC and sample payload.
   - Confirm event fields we need: prompt_id, model_tag, label, confidence, safety_tags, timestamp.

3) QMon mapping and baseline (Monica + Nova annotators) — by Wed 11/17:
   - Tag taxonomy mapping doc (clinical/intent/safety).
   - Baseline metrics computed across 1k eval items.

4) Canary policy config (Tessa + Jordan):
   - Canary traffic: 5% for 2 hours.
   - Rollback triggers (automated):
     * Absolute annotated-accuracy drop >= 3 percentage points vs baseline OR
     * Safety-tag rate increases by >= 1% absolute OR
     * Latency P95 > 2.5s for two consecutive 10-min windows.
   - If an automated trigger fires, model is immediately rolled back to previous stable tag and incident channel opens (PagerDuty + #redwood-nova-qmon).

5) Manual gating & alerts (Monica):
   - Create regression alert in Console with initial noise guard (three consecutive verdict batches showing delta).
   - Follow-up review window: 30m to 1h for human verification before customer-impacting actions when safe (but automated rollback still allowed for critical safety regressions).

6) Dry run & signoff (Marissa + Olivia) — Thu 11/19: dry-run synthetic traffic and eval event replay. Signoff required from Nova product for go-live.

References: runbook link and HubSpot deal id included below. I've attached a conservative canary-rollback-runbook-v0.2.md for your review.

Questions for Nova before kickoff:
- Can Sam confirm the webhook URL and if Redwood should validate HMAC using a shared secret?
- Are there any additional safety tags we should add to the prompt set before baseline computation?

I'll post Zoom details and a lightweight checklist to the Drive folder in the next hour.

Best,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Implementation Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0212

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@novamedical.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: QMon kickoff: initial integration plan, canary & rollback approach

Quick follow-up after reviewing the prompt set:

- I've added three additional clinical-sensitivity flags to the tag sheet (columns: PHI_LIKELIHOOD, TREATMENT_ADVICE, HIGH_RISK_PHRASE). Please confirm whether Nova wants those computed at inference-time or only as part of eval tagging. We recommend both if possible.

- For regression alerts, I'll provision the first alert with the conservative thresholds we discussed. We'll run a 72-hour monitoring window post-launch before relaxing noise guards.

- If you prefer, we can also add an early-warning signal: synthetic "canary prompts" (10 prompts injected every 15 minutes) so we get a continuous health signal during the 2-hour canary. That helps us detect regressions that the sampled eval harness might miss.

If all looks good I can create the Console alert config and the PagerDuty escalation policy template today.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Lead Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
